title: Integral conjugacy of cocharacters into a fixed split maximal torus
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with uniformizer $\pi$ and $A\simeq\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/(\pi^n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. An $A$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] with base $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A reductive $A$-group scheme here means a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme with reductive geometric fibres: over every algebraically closed field a fibre is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Write $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. For an $A$-algebra $B$, $H(B)$ means $A$-scheme morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}B\to H$, with the induced group law. A cocharacter is an $A$-group homomorphism $\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$. Let $H$ be a reductive $A$-group scheme, and let $S\hookrightarrow H$ be a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] with a specified isomorphism $S\simeq\mathbf G_{m,A}^r$, $r\geq0$, such that every geometric fibre of $S$ is a maximal torus in the corresponding fibre of $H$. A torus over an algebraically closed field is a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$, and maximal refers to inclusion of subgroup schemes. For every cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$ there exist $c\in H(A)$ and a cocharacter $\nu:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to S$ such that $c\lambda c^{-1}$ is the composite of $\nu$ and $S\hookrightarrow H$, as morphisms of $A$-group schemes. Equivalently this equality holds on all $B$-points for every commutative $A$-algebra $B$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf. Remark 3.5, forward implication, printed p.5: integral conjugation into a fixed maximal split torus. Only the complete-DVR case is needed here; the statement is the conjugacy input, not a Cartan factorization.

proof.text: Put $k=A/(\pi)$ and $H_k=H\times_A\operatorname{Spec}k$. The base-change smoothness clause of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] makes $H_k$ smooth. Writing $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$ identifies this fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\pi C)$, so it is affine of finite type. The hypothesis on geometric fibres says exactly that $H_k$ is geometrically connected and reductive. The prescribed splitting gives $S_k\simeq\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$, and geometric maximality implies maximality among $k$-split tori: an inclusion in a larger split torus would remain such an inclusion after algebraic closure. Apply [lem-sfb-field-split-torus-rational-containment] to $G=H_k$, $D=\mathbf G_{m,k}$ and $f=\lambda_k$. Obtain $c_1\in H(k)$ and $\nu_1:\mathbf G_{m,k}\to S_k$ with $c_1\lambda_kc_1^{-1}=\nu_1$.

Write each coordinate of $
u_1$ as a group-like Laurent polynomial $q(z)=\sum_j a_jz^j\in k[z,z^{-1}]$. Comparing coefficients in $q(zw)=q(z)q(w)$ gives $a_j^2=a_j$ and $a_i a_j=0$ for $i
e j$; the identity condition is $\sum_j a_j=1$. Since $k$ is a field, precisely one coefficient is $1$, and the others vanish. Thus the coordinates are $z^{e_1},\ldots,z^{e_r}$ for integers $e_i$. Define $
u:\mathbf G_{m,A}	o S$ using the same integer powers in the specified splitting. Integer powers preserve units and multiplication on every algebra, so this is an $A$-group homomorphism, and its reduction is $
u_1$. For $r=0$ it is the unique homomorphism to the trivial group.

proof.text:
On the smooth affine $A$-scheme $H$ define $t*x=
u(t)x\lambda(t)^{-1}$. This is a scheme morphism by the group operations, and $1*x=x$. Moreover $t*(u*x)=
u(t)
u(u)x\lambda(u)^{-1}\lambda(t)^{-1}=
u(tu)x\lambda(tu)^{-1}$, so it is an action of $\mathbf G_{m,A}$. A point $c$ over any $A$-algebra is fixed in the universal sense precisely when $
u(t)c=c\lambda(t)$ after every further algebra extension, equivalently $c\lambda(t)c^{-1}=
u(t)$. Step 1 says that $c_1$ is fixed for the reduction of this action to $k$.

proof.text: Set $A_n=A/(\pi^n)$ for $n\geq1$. Inductively construct fixed points $c_n\in H(A_n)$ with $c_{n+1}\bmod\pi^n=c_n$, starting with step 1. The kernel $J_n=(\pi^n)/(\pi^{n+1})$ of $A_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_n$ has square zero, since $2n\geq n+1$. Apply [lem-sfb-gm-fixed-square-zero-lifting] over the base ring $R=A$, to the smooth affine scheme $X=H$ with the action in step 3 and to this surjection. Its conclusion supplies a fixed lift $c_{n+1}$ of the particular $c_n$ already chosen, which is the required compatibility. This establishes the induction for every positive $n$ without making any assumption on the residue field.

proof.text: By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], each $c_n$ is an $A$-algebra map $C\to A_n$. Compatibility gives the $A$-algebra map $b:C\to\varprojlim_n A_n$, $h\mapsto(c_n^*(h))_n$: it preserves sums, products and scalars componentwise. Completeness [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] identifies the limit with $A$ through its canonical map, so $b$ gives $c\in H(A)$ reducing to every $c_n$. The same completeness implies $\bigcap_n\pi^n A=0$: an element in that intersection has all zero coordinates and the canonical map is injective.

proof.text: Consider the two morphisms $\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$ given by $t\mapsto c\lambda(t)c^{-1}$ and $t\mapsto\nu(t)$. Their reductions to $A_n$ agree as morphisms, because $c_n$ is fixed. On coordinate rings, for each $h\in C$ the difference of its two pullbacks is a Laurent polynomial $\sum_j b_jz^j$ whose image in $A_n[z,z^{-1}]$ is zero for every $n$. Uniqueness of Laurent coefficients gives $b_j\in\bigcap_n\pi^nA=0$ for every $j$. Thus the pullbacks agree on every $h$, hence the morphisms agree by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Composition with the closed inclusion $S\hookrightarrow H$ is understood in this equality. Equality of morphisms gives the claimed equality on all commutative $A$-algebras, including nonreduced ones. This proves the full assertion for the constructed $c$ and $\nu$.
